topics.title: Design Consistent Hashing
topics.description: Understanding consistent hashing, hash rings, virtual nodes, and how distributed systems minimize data reshuffling.

subtopics.title: Consistent Hashing
subtopics.theory:
1️⃣ Consistent Hashing

🔹 Interview Definition

Consistent hashing is a data distribution technique that maps both keys and servers onto a circular hash space (ring) to minimize data movement when servers are added or removed.

🔹 Why Needed

Normal hashing:

hash(key) % N

If N changes → almost all keys move.

Large distributed systems:

Servers join

Servers fail

Scaling happens

We need minimal reshuffling.

🔹 Important Points

Hash space is circular (ring)

Both keys and servers are hashed

Key → next clockwise server

Supports wrap-around

Minimizes rebalancing

Uses virtual nodes for load balance

🔹 Flow

Hash server IDs → place on ring

Hash keys → place on ring

For each key:

Move clockwise

First server found → assign

If server added:

Only nearby keys move

If server removed:

Keys move to next clockwise server

🔹 Advantages

Minimal key movement

High scalability

High availability

Smooth horizontal scaling

No global rehashing

Ideal for distributed systems

🔹 Disadvantages

Slightly complex implementation

Uneven load without virtual nodes

Extra memory for metadata

Requires sorted structure

subtopics.title: Hash Ring
subtopics.theory:
2️⃣ Hash Ring

🔹 Definition

A hash ring is a circular representation of the hash space where both servers and keys are mapped.

🔹 Important Points

Range typically: 0 → 2³²−1

Treated as circular

Wrap-around supported

Lookup uses clockwise search

🔹 Why Ring?

Avoids dependence on number of servers.

subtopics.title: Virtual Nodes (vNodes)
subtopics.theory:
3️⃣ Virtual Nodes (vNodes)

🔹 Interview Definition

Virtual nodes are multiple logical representations of a physical server on the hash ring to improve load balancing.

🔹 Why Needed

Without virtual nodes:

Uneven key distribution

Some servers overloaded

Hotspot problem

🔹 Important Points

One physical server → many virtual nodes

Keys map to virtual nodes

Virtual nodes map to physical server

Improves uniform distribution

Enables weighted load balancing

🔹 Flow

For each server:

Create multiple virtual nodes

Hash each virtual node

Insert into ring

Key assigned to virtual node

🔹 Advantages

Balanced load

Smooth scaling

Better fault tolerance

Supports heterogeneous servers

🔹 Disadvantages

More memory usage

More metadata

Slightly more complex

subtopics.title: Add Server
subtopics.theory:
4️⃣ Add Server

🔹 Flow

Create virtual nodes

Hash and insert into ring

Identify previous node

Move keys in range:

(previous → new node]

Other keys unchanged

🔹 Important Point

Only local range of keys move.

subtopics.title: Remove Server
subtopics.theory:
5️⃣ Remove Server

🔹 Flow

Identify all virtual nodes

Remove from ring

Keys move to next clockwise node

🔹 Important Point

No global reshuffling.

subtopics.title: Data Structure Used
subtopics.theory:
6️⃣ Data Structure Used

🔹 Sorted Map / TreeMap

Why?

Maintains order

Allows clockwise lookup

Supports:

insert

delete

search

🔹 Complexity

Lookup: O(log N)

Add/remove: O(V log N)

V = virtual nodes count

subtopics.title: Real-World Usage
subtopics.theory:
7️⃣ Real-World Usage

Used in:

Distributed cache (Redis, Memcached)

Load balancers

Sharded databases

Distributed storage systems

Web crawlers

subtopics.title: Important Definitions
subtopics.theory:
8️⃣ Important Definitions (Must Know Words)

🔹 Hash Function

Function that converts input into fixed-size numeric value.

🔹 Hash Space

Range of possible hash outputs.

🔹 Hash Ring

Circular representation of hash space.

🔹 Clockwise Lookup

Finding first server moving clockwise from key.

🔹 Rebalancing

Moving keys between servers when cluster changes.

🔹 Virtual Node

Logical node representing physical server on ring.

🔹 Horizontal Scaling

Adding more machines instead of increasing machine power.

🔹 Hotspot

Server receiving disproportionate traffic.

🔹 Resharding

Redistributing data when shards change.

subtopics.title: Chapter Summary
subtopics.theory:
🎯 Short Chapter Summary

Consistent hashing distributes keys across a circular hash ring so that only a small number of keys move when servers are added or removed, using virtual nodes to maintain balanced load distribution.
